author: Mark Atwood
text:
The bead itself recommends lifting to a workspace-level epic rather than a per-crate fix, and the parent JMAP-sgrr review notes explicitly flag the workspace-policy ambiguity ('If a future contributor disagrees with sgrr.27 on policy grounds, closing it as not-a-bug is fine; the finding documents the trade-off').

This is a real workspace-architectural decision with three plausible answers:

  (a) Ship constructors workspace-wide. Add fn new(mandatory_fields) -> Self on every public #[non_exhaustive] wire-format struct in jmap-types, jmap-mail-types, jmap-chat-types, jmap-calendars-types, jmap-tasks-types, jmap-contacts-types, jmap-filenode-types, jmap-sharing-types, jmap-metadata-types, jmap-jscalendar-types, jmap-jscontact-types, jmap-cid-types. Big epic (~30 crates, hundreds of types). Establishes a 'kit ships ergonomic construction' posture.

  (b) Ship #[doc(hidden)] test-only constructors plus document the deserialize-only public construction path. Acknowledges that external crates can construct via serde_json::from_value, makes that the explicit recommended path, and adds Default impls where mandatory fields permit. Smaller epic.

  (c) Status quo + close as not-a-bug. The kit's posture is that consumers compose via deserialize, not via direct struct-literal construction. The workspace AGENTS.md kit-vs-jig section emphasises the kit-as-building-blocks posture, which is more consistent with 'deserialize is the construction API' than 'every struct has a constructor'. Document this stance in a workspace AGENTS.md section.

Recommendation: option (c). Rationale:
  - The kit is wire-format types. Construction-via-JSON is the spec-aligned way to build a wire object: every test in the workspace uses hand-written JSON with from_value. The fluent-Rust constructor path would be a parallel ergonomic surface that callers wouldn't trust as much (the JSON oracle is the spec; a constructor is the kit's interpretation).
  - Constructors on partial-response-Option fields create a contradiction: callers can build a Calendar with kind=None / uri=None that round-trips through wire to a spec-non-conformant peer (this is exactly bd:JMAP-sgrr.17's concern, also human-filed).
  - The workspace canonical-template rule + the size of (a) (hundreds of types, every sibling crate touched) is a large cost for an ergonomic improvement that bypasses the deserialize path the kit is built around.
  - (b) is reasonable middle ground but requires inventing a 'recommended construction path' that doesn't currently exist; the rustdoc work is non-trivial.

If you pick (a) or (b), file as a fresh workspace-level epic (not JMAP-sgrr.27.* — it doesn't belong as a child of the jscontact-types-only review epic).

If you pick (c), close JMAP-sgrr.27 with reason citing the workspace kit posture, and add a paragraph to workspace AGENTS.md ('Public-API construction: prefer deserialize-from-JSON over struct-literal or constructor on public wire-format types; constructor methods are a deliberate omission').
